archetypes.name: caller-inventory
archetypes.rationale: Plan claims exactly three run-external-agent.sh callers need --stderr-sink; unverified omissions would silently leave more lanes broken.
archetypes.prompt_body: Search the entire repository for every invocation of run-external-agent.sh and every direct call to select_failed_agent_stderr_source to verify the plan's assertion that only three callers (launch-codex-implement.sh, lint-fix-loop.sh, review-and-fix.sh) are broken default-mode lanes. For each caller not listed in the plan, determine whether its fd2 destination makes it a broken lane (custom sink, needs --stderr-sink) or an intentionally excluded lane (capture-mode, .sidecar convention, or Cursor). Also check whether any test harness, CI script, or wrapper under scripts/ or skills/ invokes run-external-agent.sh and whether those invocations would require or should be updated to test the new flag. An undiscovered broken lane would mean the fix is incomplete for that lane's .stderr-tail consumers even after this PR lands. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sink-predicate
archetypes.rationale: The [[ -s ]] guard silently falls through to .diag when the explicit sink is empty, and validate_meta_scalar_path runs before the file exists; both semantics need plan-level justification.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's choice of [[ -s "$explicit_sink" ]] as the gate for the explicit-sink priority branch in select_failed_agent_stderr_source. Determine whether an empty-but-present custom sink (agent produced no stderr output) should still take explicit priority over .sidecar/.diag fallbacks, or whether silently skipping it to fall back to .diag boilerplate is the correct operator experience when a sink is explicitly declared. Also examine whether validate_meta_scalar_path validating --stderr-sink before the agent runs (when the file does not yet exist) matches the validator's actual character-allowlist or existence semantics, and whether it could incorrectly reject or accept valid launcher-produced paths that happen not to exist at parse time. Check the existing --output validation for comparison to confirm the plan's claim that --stderr-sink validation is truly symmetric. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
